verses.1: For the leader; according to "Lilies." Eduth. A psalm of Asaph.
verses.2: Shepherd of Israel, listen, guide of the flock of Joseph! From your throne upon the cherubim reveal yourself
verses.3: to Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Stir up your power, come to save us.
verses.4: O LORD of hosts, restore us; Let your face shine upon us, that we may be saved.
verses.5: LORD of hosts, how long will you burn with anger while your people pray?
verses.6: You have fed them the bread of tears, made them drink tears in abundance.
verses.7: You have left us to be fought over by our neighbors; our enemies deride us.
verses.8: O LORD of hosts, restore us; let your face shine upon us, that we may be saved.
verses.9: You brought a vine out of Egypt; you drove away the nations and planted it.
verses.10: You cleared the ground; it took root and filled the land.
verses.11: The mountains were covered by its shadow, the cedars of God by its branches.
verses.12: It sent out boughs as far as the sea, shoots as far as the river.
verses.13: Why have you broken down the walls, so that all who pass by pluck its fruit?
verses.14: The boar from the forest strips the vine; the beast of the field feeds upon it.
verses.15: Turn again, LORD of hosts; look down from heaven and see; Attend to this vine,
verses.16: the shoot your right hand has planted.
verses.17: Those who would burn or cut it down - may they perish at your rebuke.
verses.18: May your help be with the man at your right hand, with the one whom you once made strong.
verses.19: Then we will not withdraw from you; revive us, and we will call on your name.
verses.20: LORD of hosts, restore us; let your face shine upon us, that we may be saved.

notes.text: Lilies.... Eduth: the first term is probably the title of the melody to which the psalm was to be sung; the second is unexplained.
A vine: a frequent metaphor for Israel. Cf Isaiah 5:1-7; 27:2-5; Jeremiah 2:21; Hosea 10:1; Matthew 21:33.

The sea: the Mediterranean. The river: the Euphrates. Cf Genesis 15:18; 1 Kings 5:1. The terms may also have a mythic nuance - the seas that surround the earth; sea and river are sometimes paralleled in poetry.
The man at your right hand... the one: the Davidic king who will lead the army in battle.
